# AgentHub Documentation

What AgentHub does, and every endpoint it answers.

> Ships with this console build

## Concepts

AgentHub registers five kinds of resource plus a custom lane, then runs them over A2A. Every call resolves to one resource, produces one task, and reports one health value that it actually measured.

### Resource lanes

| Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| Model | A provider behind an OpenAI-compatible chat completions API. |
| Agent | A remote agent that publishes an A2A Agent Card. |
| MCP | An MCP server reached over stdio or streamable HTTP. |
| Skill | A packaged instruction set an agent can load. |
| CLI | A local command, run only when it is on the allowlist. |
| Custom | Anything else you want to register and route to. |

### Task lifecycle

`Submitted → Working → Input required → Completed | Failed | Canceled`

A task parked in input-required waits indefinitely. Resume it with tasks/resume and the same task id.

### Health

**Healthy** · **Degraded** · **Unhealthy** · **Unknown**

A health value is only ever written by a probe or a run. Nothing declares itself healthy, so an unmeasured resource stays unknown.

### Record status

`Draft → Pending → Approved → Rejected | Deprecated`

draft to pending to approved, then deprecated. Only approved records are discoverable and exported.

## A2A methods

A single JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint answers every method below. The HTTP status stays 200 even when the task fails: read result.state, not the status line.

| Method | What it does | Params | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message/send` | Run one turn and wait for the terminal state. | `{ message, configuration?, metadata? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: Task }` |
| `message/stream` | The same turn, with frames streamed as it progresses. | `{ message, configuration?, metadata? }` | `text/event-stream: task_status_update \| task_artifact_update \| message \| task_span_update` |
| `tasks/get` | Read a task together with its history. | `{ id, taskId?, historyLength?, metadata? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: Task }` |
| `tasks/cancel` | Cancel a task that is still running. | `{ id, taskId?, historyLength?, metadata? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: Task }` |
| `tasks/resume` | Answer a task that is parked waiting for input. | `{ id, taskId?, message, metadata? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: Task }` |
| `tasks/pushNotification/set` | Register the callback a task should notify. | `{ taskId, id?, pushNotificationConfig? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: PushNotificationConfig }` |
| `tasks/pushNotification/get` | Read the callback registered for a task. | `{ id, taskId? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: PushNotificationConfig }` |

The stream ends on the terminal status frame; there is no sentinel frame after it.

### v0.1 aliases

- `tasks/send` → `message/send`
- `tasks/sendSubscribe` → `message/stream`

### Shapes

**Message**

```json
{
  "kind": "message",
  "role": "user",
  "messageId": "…",
  "parts": [
    { "kind": "text", "type": "text", "text": "probe google-adk" }
  ]
}
```

**Task**

```json
{
  "kind": "task",
  "id": "task-ff5eba3cefe2be87",
  "status": {
    "state": "completed",
    "message": { "role": "agent", "parts": [{ "type": "text", "text": "…" }] }
  },
  "artifacts": [
    { "artifactId": "agent.a2a-0", "name": "agent.a2a", "parts": [{ "type": "data", "data": { … } }] }
  ],
  "history": [{ "role": "user", "parts": [{ "type": "text", "text": "…" }] }]
}
```

## HTTP API

The control plane the console itself talks to. Routes marked `public` are anonymous; routes marked `session` need a signed-in session but no permission code; every other route needs a session cookie plus the permission named in the column. A delete answers the way a read does: an id the caller cannot see is 404, whether it is already gone or belongs to somebody else. The console treats that answer as already done.

### Base URL

The console, the A2A endpoint and every control-plane path share one listener. The address below is the default; the environment variable beside it overrides that port. Compose also publishes the development database on its own host port.

```text
http://localhost:3500          AGENTHUB_HTTP_PORT (default)
localhost:5434                 POSTGRES_PORT (compose development database only)
```

### Protocol

| Method | Path | Permission | What it does | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/.well-known/agent.json` | `public` | The A2A Agent Card: where discovery starts. | — | `AgentCard { name, description, url, version, protocolVersion, capabilities, skills[] }` |
| `GET` | `/a2a/agent-card` | `public` | The same card served on a second path. | — | `AgentCard` |
| `POST` | `/a2a` | `public` | One JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint carrying every A2A method. | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, method: "message/send", params }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result } \| { jsonrpc: "2.0", id, error: { code, message } }` |
| `GET` | `/a2a/stream` | `tasks:read` — Read tasks | Server-sent events for one task. | `?task=<id>&since=<seq>` | `text/event-stream, keep-alive every 15s` |

### Users

| Method | Path | Permission | What it does | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/users` | `users:manage` — Manage users | List all users | `?q=` | `{ users: [{ id, email, name, status, isOwner, roles, groups }] }` |
| `POST` | `/api/users` | `users:manage` — Manage users | Create a new entry among the users | `{ email, password, name, status?, roles[], groups[] }` | `{ user } — 201` |
| `GET` | `/api/users/{id}` | `users:manage` — Manage users | Read one of the users by id | — | `{ user }` |
| `PUT` | `/api/users/{id}` | `users:manage` — Manage users | Replace one of the users outright | `{ email?, name?, password?, status?, roles[]?, groups[]? }` | `{ user }` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/users/{id}` | `users:manage` — Manage users | Delete one of the users | — | `204, no body` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/users/{id}/sessions` | `sessions:manage` — Revoke sessions | Revoke every session belonging to one user. | — | `204, no body` |

Deleting a user is a soft delete: the row is kept so the audit trail, tasks and grants that name it survive, and every live session is revoked so a deleted identity cannot keep working. The account’s status becomes `deleted` — distinct from `disabled`, which is a reversible lockout. Enable and Disable flip status between `active` and `disabled` via `PUT /api/users/{id}`; a soft-deleted account can be re-enabled the same way.

### Backups

| Method | Path | Permission | What it does | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/backups` | `backups:manage` — Manage database checkpoints | Whether backups are on, plus every checkpoint. | — | `{ enabled, reason?, engine?, nextRun?, activeTasks, checkpoints: [], keepLast, maxAgeDays }` |
| `POST` | `/api/backups` | `backups:manage` — Manage database checkpoints | Take a checkpoint now. | `{ label? }` | `{ checkpoint } — 201` |
| `GET` | `/api/backups/schedule` | `backups:manage` — Manage database checkpoints | Read the checkpoint schedule. | — | `{ schedule: { mode, enabled, intervalSec, dailyTime, timezone, cronExpr, keepLast, maxAgeDays, nextRun? } }` |
| `PUT` | `/api/backups/schedule` | `backups:manage` — Manage database checkpoints | Save the checkpoint schedule. | `{ mode, enabled, intervalSec, dailyTime, timezone, cronExpr, keepLast, maxAgeDays }` | `{ schedule }` |
| `GET` | `/api/backups/{id}` | `backups:manage` — Manage database checkpoints | Read one of the checkpoints by id | — | `{ id, kind, engine, status, sizeBytes, rowCount, checksum, createdAt }` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/backups/{id}` | `backups:manage` — Manage database checkpoints | Delete one of the checkpoints | — | `204, no body` |
| `GET` | `/api/backups/{id}/download` | `backups:manage` — Manage database checkpoints | Download one checkpoint archive. | — | `application/gzip` |
| `POST` | `/api/backups/{id}/restore` | `backups:manage` — Manage database checkpoints | Restore a checkpoint; confirm echoes its id. | `{ confirm } — must echo the checkpoint id` | `{ checkpoint }` |

A checkpoint carries application tables only: the catalogue and the append-only audit ledger are neither dumped nor truncated, so a rewind keeps both the archive’s own record and the trail it restores around. The built-in engine empties the schema with one TRUNCATE, so a table guarded by a BEFORE TRUNCATE trigger is refused with backup_table_guarded — use the pg_dump engine where such a table exists.

| `GET` | `/api/computers/{id}` | `resources:read` — Read resources | Read one of the computers by id | — | `Computer \| 404 computer_not_found` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/computers/{id}` | `resources:write` — Change resources | Delete one of the computers | — | `204 — terminates the sandbox lease first, then drops the card \| 404 computer_not_found` |
| `GET` | `/api/schedules` | `tasks:read` — Read tasks | List all schedules | — | `Schedule[] { id, goal, trigger(manual\|cron\|event), cronExpr, enabled, nextRun, lastRunAt, lastStatus }` |
| `POST` | `/api/schedules` | `tasks:write` — Cancel and resume tasks | Create a new entry among the schedules | `{ goal(required), trigger?(manual\|cron\|event), cronExpr?, enabled? } — empty goal is 400 schedule_invalid` | `Schedule — 201` |
| `GET` | `/api/schedules/{id}` | `tasks:read` — Read tasks | Read one of the schedules by id | — | `Schedule \| 404 schedule_not_found` |
| `PUT` | `/api/schedules/{id}` | `tasks:write` — Cancel and resume tasks | Replace one of the schedules outright | `{ goal?, trigger?, cronExpr?, enabled? }` | `Schedule \| 404 schedule_not_found` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/schedules/{id}` | `tasks:write` — Cancel and resume tasks | Delete one of the schedules | — | `204 \| 404 schedule_not_found` |
| `GET` | `/api/knowledge` | `resources:read` — Read resources | List all knowledge | `?agentId=` | `Knowledge[] { id, agentId, chunkText, sourceRef, createdAt }` |

### Execution sandboxes

| Method | Path | Permission | What it does | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/sandboxes` | `resources:read` — Read resources | List all leases | — | `{ leases: Lease[], default: Profile, live: boolean } — Lease { id, ownerId, resourceId, scope, provider, runtime?, nodeId?, state, ref?, profile, createdAt, renewedAt, expiresAt, execs, lastExitCode, lastCommand? }` |
| `GET` | `/api/sandboxes/{id}` | `resources:read` — Read resources | Read one of the leases by id | — | `{ lease: Lease, execs: ExecRecord[] } — the last 50 executions; someone else's lease reads as 404 sandbox_not_found` |
| `GET` | `/api/sandboxes/stats` | `resources:read` — Read resources | Water level: active leases, queued jobs, nodes online, recent executions, last sweep. | — | `{ activeLeases, pendingJobs, onlineNodes, recentExecs, lastSweepAt, sweeps, reclaimed, lastError? }` |
| `GET` | `/api/sandboxes/events` | `resources:read` — Read resources | SSE: replay from `since`, then follow lease and job events live. | `?since=<seq>` | `text/event-stream, event name sandbox_event` |
| `POST` | `/api/sandboxes/{id}/exec` | `resources:write` — Change resources | Run one command inside the lease without a shell: argv is exec-ed directly, output is capped, and the receipt is audited. | `{ command(required), args?, stdin?, dir?, env?, timeoutMs? } — 1 MiB body cap; argv is exec-ed directly, never through a shell` | `ExecResult { exitCode, stdout?, stderr?, truncated, durationMs, provider, ref?, receipt? } \| 400 sandbox_policy_denied \| 409 sandbox_lease_lost \| 504 sandbox_timeout` |
| `POST` | `/api/sandboxes/{id}/renew` | `resources:write` — Change resources | Extend a lease up to the instance TTL; an expired or terminated lease cannot come back. | — | `Lease \| 409 sandbox_lease_lost (expired, terminated, or past the instance TTL)` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/sandboxes/{id}` | `resources:write` — Change resources | Delete one of the leases | — | `204, no body \| 404 sandbox_not_found` |
| `GET` | `/api/sandbox-providers` | `resources:read` — Read resources | List all sandbox providers | — | `{ providers: ProviderInfo[], groups: [{ layer, providers }], layers: Layer[], default: string }` |
| `POST` | `/api/sandbox-providers/refresh` | `resources:write` — Change resources | Re-probe every runtime, so a freshly installed container engine shows up without a restart. | — | `same shape as GET /api/sandbox-providers` |
| `GET` | `/api/sandbox-nodes` | `resources:read` — Read resources | List all execution nodes | — | `{ nodes: Node[], waiters, pollHint } — Node { id, ownerId, name, apiKeyId?, capabilities?, status, lastSeenAt, createdAt }` |
| `POST` | `/api/sandbox-nodes` | `resources:write` — Change resources | Enrol a node by id; registering the same id again updates it instead of adding a row. | `{ id(required, 1-64 of [A-Za-z0-9._-]), name?, capabilities? } — 64 KiB body cap` | `Node \| 400 bad_request \| 404 sandbox_not_found (that id belongs to someone else)` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/sandbox-nodes/{id}` | `resources:write` — Change resources | Delete one of the execution nodes | — | `204, no body \| 404 sandbox_not_found` |
| `POST` | `/api/sandbox-nodes/{id}/heartbeat` | `tasks:write` — Cancel and resume tasks | Node heartbeat; the reply carries the poll hint for the next job wait. | — | `{ node: Node, pollHint } \| 404 sandbox_not_found` |
| `GET` | `/api/sandbox-nodes/{id}/jobs` | `tasks:write` — Cancel and resume tasks | Long poll for the next job: 204 when the queue is empty for the whole wait. | `?wait=<seconds> — default 25, capped at 60` | `Job \| 204 when the queue stays empty for the whole wait` |
| `POST` | `/api/sandbox-nodes/{id}/jobs/{job}` | `tasks:write` — Cancel and resume tasks | Report a finished job back to the server; a non-empty error marks it failed. | `{ exitCode, stdout?, stderr?, truncated?, durationMs?, receipt?, error? } — 1 MiB body cap` | `{ ok: true } \| 404 sandbox_not_found` |

| Method | Path | Permission | What it does | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/audit` | `audit:read` — Read the audit trail | List all audit events | `?from=&to=&actor=&action=&resource=&source=&outcome=&q=&before=&limit=` | `{ events: AuditEvent[], stats: { total, failed, denied, written }, next }` |

Request and response shapes are listed in the last two columns of each table.

## Authentication and permissions

Identity comes from a session cookie, authorisation from permissions resolved once per request. Per-resource grants narrow this further.

### Sessions

POST /api/auth/login sets an http-only cookie. An OAuth round trip starts at /api/auth/oauth/{provider} and lands back on the callback.

### Sign-up and first login

Self-service sign-up is available when AGENTHUB_ALLOW_REGISTRATION is on. A password must be at least 8 bytes, the address must look like an address, and the first account on an empty instance becomes the owner. Accounts created this way - and accounts a first OAuth login provisions - start on the read-only viewer role: they read the catalogue and nothing more until an administrator widens them. Accounts created through POST /api/users get exactly the roles that were asked for.

### Permissions

A route is guarded by one permission or a list, and any single one of them is enough to enter.

The owner account holds every known permission and bypasses the matrix entirely.

### Groups

A group carries roles and its members inherit them, so naming a group once beats ticking the same roles on every user; a group is also a principal that resource grants can point at. Renaming it or changing its roles takes effect on the next request. Sending roles: [] clears the bundle; omitting the field leaves it alone.

### API keys

A key is a long-lived bearer credential that authenticates as its owner but only with the permissions chosen at creation. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer ahk_…` on /api routes, or as `X-AgentHub-Key`, and on the A2A endpoint.

Scope a key to the least permission it needs; a key can never be granted more than its owner holds. Treat the token as a secret — it is shown once and only its hash is stored.

## Execution sandboxes

Every agent action that touches the outside world runs inside a leased environment. The brain decides; the hands are a container, a user-space kernel, a microVM, a process sandbox or a node you enrolled — the control plane never runs anything as the host process.

| Layer | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `container` | Docker or rootless podman: one namespace-isolated container per lease, read-only root, tmpfs scratch, and no network unless the resource asked for it. The default. |
| `usermode-kernel` | runsc (gVisor) interposes a user-space kernel, so a container escape lands in Go rather than in the host kernel. |
| `microvm` | Kata or Firecracker: a real boundary per lease, at the cost of a boot on creation. |
| `process` | bubblewrap, nsjail, isolate: namespaces and seccomp without a container runtime. Cheaper, and only as strong as the host kernel. |
| `platform` | A hosted runtime (E2B, Daytona, CubeSandbox, OpenHands) reached through a declarative template: no vendor SDK is compiled in. |
| `remote` | A node you enrolled — agentbuddy on your own machine. The server queues a job and the node runs it inside its own root and allowlist. |
| `none` | off refuses every execution. Nothing runs, and the console says so instead of falling back. |

### Resource execution policy

A resource that runs something can narrow the instance default through kind_config.sandbox. Every field is optional: an absent field inherits what the operator set, so a resource can lower a limit but never raise one by omission. The block is validated when the record is saved, not when a task first runs into it.

`kind_config.sandbox` · `agent` · `mcp` · `cli`

```json
{
  "kind": "cli",
  "name": "ruff",
  "kind_config": {
    "sandbox": {
      "provider": "docker",
      "runtime": "runsc",
      "image": "python:3.12-slim",
      "work_dir": "/work",
      "readonly_root": false,
      "network": "none",
      "cpu": 1.5,
      "memory_mb": 512,
      "pids_limit": 128,
      "timeout_ms": 30000,
      "max_output_bytes": 262144,
      "env_allowlist": ["PATH", "HOME"],
      "args_policy": "prefix",
      "args_allowlist": ["--check", "--select"]
    }
  }
}
```

Network is the one field that is not a promise of reach. Only bridge and platform hand out connectivity; egress_allowlist records the hosts a resource would like and is executed as none until an egress proxy exists, because accepting the value must not turn into a filter that is not there. readonly_root is tri-state: unset inherits a read-only root, and an explicit false is the only way to ask for a writable one.

### Network modes

| Mode | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | No interface at all. An empty or unrecognised value becomes this too, because a typo must not turn into network access. |
| `egress_allowlist` | A host list, kept so existing records still parse. Executed as none: no provider filters hosts yet, so neither backend grants connectivity for it. |
| `bridge` | A NAT'd interface with outbound access and no route in. A container gets its own bridge; bubblewrap shares the host's network namespace. |
| `platform` | Whatever the host runtime calls its default. A container gets the daemon's bridge; bubblewrap shares the host network. |

## Errors

Failures answer with a machine-readable code. Grouped here by the HTTP status they map to.

| Status | Meaning | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | Bad Request | `bad_request, weak_password, invalid_email, invalid_grant, unknown_permission, password_required, backup_schedule_invalid, restore_confirm_required, schedule_invalid, router_policy_invalid, channel_payload_invalid, connector_action_denied, audio_unsupported, sandbox_unknown_provider, api_key_name_required, api_key_invalid_scope` |
| `401` | Unauthorized | `unauthorized, unauthenticated, session_expired, invalid_credentials, channel_signature_missing, channel_signature_invalid, channel_timestamp_expired, api_key_expired, api_key_revoked` |
| `403` | Forbidden | `forbidden, user_disabled, builtin_role, skill_distill_disabled, channel_disabled, connector_policy_off, sandbox_disabled, sandbox_policy_denied` |
| `404` | Not Found | `not_found, backup_not_found, computer_not_found, schedule_not_found, router_ticket_not_found, router_trigger_not_found, router_thread_not_found, channel_not_found, delivery_not_found, connector_not_found, sandbox_not_found, file_not_found, connector_approval_not_found, api_key_not_found` |
| `405` | Method Not Allowed | `method_not_allowed` |
| `409` | Conflict | `email_taken, role_already_exists, group_already_exists, backups_disabled, backup_in_progress, backup_checksum_mismatch, backup_schema_mismatch, backup_invalid_archive, backup_table_guarded, router_ticket_closed, router_handback_exhausted, router_resource_unset, delivery_not_retryable, sandbox_unsupported, sandbox_lease_lost, sandbox_capability_unavailable, connector_approval_closed` |
| `413` | Payload Too Large | `payload_too_large, audio_too_large, file_too_large` |
| `415` | Unsupported Media Type | `audio_unsupported, file_unsupported` |
| `422` | Unprocessable Entity | `audio_transcribe_failed` |
| `429` | Too Many Requests | `account_locked, sandbox_limit_reached` |
| `500` | Internal Server Error | `internal_error, backup_engine_failed, backup_failed, backup_interrupted, restore_failed` |
| `502` | Bad Gateway | `oauth_not_configured, oauth_state_mismatch, oauth_failed, oauth_no_email, delivery_failed, file_store_error` |
| `503` | Service Unavailable | `backup_engine_unavailable, restore_busy, restore_in_progress, feature_unavailable, speech_disabled, sandbox_node_offline, files_disabled` |
| `504` | Gateway Timeout | `sandbox_timeout` |

The body is always {"code": "..."}. Log the code rather than any prose that came with it.

### Adapter codes

| Codes | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `resource_unreachable` | The resource never answered. |
| `adapter_timeout` | The call did not come back inside its budget. |
| `provider_malformed` | It answered, but in a shape nothing could use. |
| `provider_unauthorized` | It answered, and rejected the credentials. |
| `cli_command_not_allowed` | The command is missing from the allowlist. |
| `unknown_kind` | No adapter is registered for this kind. |
